text: Check your surroundings and ensure your vessel is not at risk of collision or grounding. If possible, make sure you are anchored to avoid drifting into a shoreline or another vessel. If at night, make sure your vessel’s lights stay on and are appropriately lit. Keep a sharp lookout and be aware of potentially dangerous situations. Monitor weather conditions.

Check your bilge and below-deck compartments to make sure your vessel is not taking on water. Check for visible damage to the vessel’s hull and along the waterline, both inside and outside the vessel, as best as possible. Check your engine for any damage or potential fire hazards.
Ensure that all members of your crew or passengers have not suffered any injuries or are at risk of a medical emergency.
Have your phone and VHF radio turned on, volume up, and available at all times. Please conserve your phone battery and any onboard power sources.

Contact the appropriate response service provider as soon as possible. Please provide the dispatcher and/or captain, OR emergency response personnel, with all the requested information about your vessel, current situation, current location, and/or any other important details. Please provide all vital information regarding the nature of the vessel's distress, and how/why/when the events occurred. Please update if any other issues arise.

Check that there are no ropes/lines, swimmers/persons, or significant debris in the water next to your vessel that may impede the assistance vessel from safely coming alongside your vessel. If possible, remove any significant debris and/or alert the incoming response vessel prior to arrival.
